I really need a "mid" option. Gave this a try after burning through Aniimo really quick, trying out different games in the genre and all that and, jeeze, what it a rough transition. The combat is ass, the pals are dumb as rocks and will repeatedly shoot into the dirt, and unless you are mounted many wild pals will just run away from you from quite a long distance so catching things can be pretty annoying, especially pre mounts. Exploration feel pretty mediocer too. The interface is also pretty clunky. It's not refund worthy, just dissapointing compared to other games in the creature catching genre. The main redeeming quality so far is the base building is decently interesting I guess. It's fun watching everyone go around and brutalize the landscape, cook, ect. So far far it feels like it's the actual main draw, maybe exploration gets more fun later too, certainly a lot of territory to travel. The combat, though, god the combat is so bad.

Rust+Pokemon+Breath of the Wild, clearly. It gives you tons of choices. You can't really be a pacifist, but you can play this like a traditional pokemon game where you catch far more than you hunt and pour more time into your base building. The best buffed meals require you do some hunting or ranching as the traders that would sell it to you appear randomly, rarely. Excellent single player experience which makes it 10/10 for me, without a doubt; pokemon has a lot it can learn from this game. There's some jankiness here and there but the game is exceptionally well balanced with a reasonable progression.

The game shows its early access roots, but in a good way -- the higher-level regions look progressively more interesting, have interesting mechanics, and have better music. The final area of the game looks amazing, sounds beautiful, and has accordingly strong, rewarding drops and loot. The starter area is fairly boring but gives you plenty of time and space to figure out how you want to play.

If there's one issue/problem I've found, the arena is designed rather poorly. Clearly an afterthought. It's fun for the first couple battles, but it just turns into a meaningless grind afterwards if you're looking for the achievements or reusable implants. The final difficulty with maxed out pals and the strongest buffs in the game seems to be a 50/50 success, and the reward after the first win is like 10% better. Total nonsense. The second to last difficulty is incredibly easy with the same squad. So just spam that one instead. Maybe with an ideal pal composition you'll spend 10% less time maxing out your rank but I doubt it. It'll probably take more time to build that pal composition.

[h1]★ ★ ★ ★ ☆ – Pok3mon with Assault Rifles and Tax Fraud[/h1]

[h3]The Good Stuff:[/h3]
* [b]Unapologetic Chaos:[/b] Exploring, catching cute creatures, and immediately putting them to work in an automated ammunition assembly line is oddly satisfying.
* [b]The Combat:[/b] Nothing beats the sheer hilarity of a boss fight where your primary strategy is hiding behind a boulder while your pet penguin fires a rocket launcher.

[h3]The Late-Game Reality Check:[/h3]
However, the further you go, the more the game transforms from a fun adventure into a grueling [b]second full-time job[/b]. The endgame loop becomes a massive, soul-crushing grind for rare resources where you will spend hours staring at automated furnaces just to craft a single set of legendary armor—which can get incredibly tedious and annoying on a long-term playthrough.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Verdict:[/b] [i]Highly recommended, until the crippling industrial management burnout sets in.[/i]

Overall a great open World survival Craft (pokemon) Game with a lot to accomplish & explore but very little details in the World and especially with NPC`s. If you like Survival Craft Games  or if youre just a Pokemon fan like my little Brother, then Palworld is for you. And  Dont get me wrong i really like this Game but Thats why i have to critisize it a little harsh here. 

I know the Focus isn`t on World or NPC building but more on Pals / craft / survival / battle but the world still feels a little barren and / or empty sometimes.
The NPC`s and their Factions feel like they were thrown in there last second. The Game doesnt even acknowledge that there are Enemy Bases. There is no Point to doing them except for some trashy loot you  will never need. No Quest. no Mentioning. Nothing. Why are there so many Factions with their own Goals but they dont do anything about it. Other NPC`s tell us about their Goals. Thats it. no more info. Same with dungeons. We get informed what they are. Done. No more quests or mentions about dungeons and they too arent needed that much except for some farming (fcking Heal shrooms!) /  mining. The World building / engagement definetly got skipped in some Places for more focus on the Pals. 

NOW LET`S TALK ABOUT THE ENDGAME:

Who tf thought this was a fun Idea for the Endgame Loop?!
Running around the Worldtree for Hours just so i can get some holy Water, craft something at the Base and immediately run back to the Tree for some more Water?!
Yeah you can UP how much you Farm with pal Builds but its still the most boring Endgame Loop i have ever seen and i hate to say that it killed the fun i had with the Game. More on that further down...

The difficulties are also a joke.
Normal Mode is perfect for your first run but Hard Mode?! WTF is that?!
Fully geared Character, Maxxed health, fully leveled, modified and bred Pals and most bosses still kill you with 2 Hits. Also; Quests dont reactivate and only bosses can be done again. I would love to see a New Game+ Mode where you can start over  and not just run around the World tree for Hours and Hours to kill all the Pals for some Water, to upgrade some Stuff, level some Pals and then try the Boss again. For me as a Solo Player, it just wasnt fun or engaging anymore. Grounded did the New Game+ the best in my Opinion. Just a new start with everything you already achieved and gathered. I really wish Palworld would implement that as well or i sadly dont see a Reason to come back to play some more. 

It still was an awesome experience and i wish Pocketpair all the best for their Future.

As someone who's really not a big fan of Pokemon, this was the kind of spin that was needed to get me into it.  Fighting with pals made all the difference.  Having your own character with it's own build and stuff really made combat more engaging.  And while I did like the survival/builder aspect, I think this is probably the game's weakest point.  In other builder games there's usually a point where you have everything automated.  That does not happen in this game.  You're always expected to sit there and manage all your bases.  And it's kind of misleading in the trailer when it shows a conveyor belt when in reality that's just another crafting table.  There's no way to automate the creation of items, have those items go down a conveyor to be combined at another point and eventually be deposited in a chest.  EVERYTHING needs to be made manually.  Every step of the way.  And that sucks at the end of the game when you need like... a ton of AI cores.  But either way, had a lot of fun with this and a couple of friends.
